rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: An airspace infringement is an unauthorised entry into notified airspace, including controlled, prohibited, restricted or special-use airspace and designated aerodrome or transponder zones.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: Around 1,100 airspace infringements are reported each year through the Mandatory Occurrence Reporting scheme.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: Every airspace infringement has potential to create a significant safety risk and operational disruption.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: CAA CAP 1840 provides current practical guidance and key information for avoiding airspace infringements.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: CAA prevention training covers airspace structure, pre-flight planning, airmanship, in-flight practices, monitoring codes, transponders and moving-map use.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: CAA CAP 2125 addresses common myths, factual planning requirements, immediate follow-up and decision-making after an infringement.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: CAA CAP 1404 defines the review and remedial-action process used after reported airspace infringements.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: Safety reporting supports collection, analysis and learning, while just-culture principles distinguish honest error from gross negligence or wilful violation.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: Airspace-infringement risk depends on route planning, airspace complexity, weather, visibility, navigation equipment, pilot workload, competence, radio use and in-flight decision-making.

rows.source: CAA airspace-infringement prevention and review
rows.verified: CAA infringement evidence is flight-, pilot-, airspace-, equipment-, operation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level aviation-event probability.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: MCA MGN 592 Amendment 2 provides current guidance on safe installation, inspection, maintenance and use of anchoring, mooring, towing and hauling equipment.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: Mooring, anchoring, towing and hauling operations can impose very large loads and should be assessed as complete systems rather than as isolated components.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: Relevant systems include winches, bollards, fairleads, ropes, wires, chains and their structural attachments to the vessel.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: Risk assessment should consider shoreside equipment, snap-back and sudden line-tension hazards, work positioning, communication and equipment condition.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: The 2026 Code of Safe Working Practices is the MCA's authoritative best-practice manual and must be accessible on UK-flagged merchant ships within its scope.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: MCA MGN 591 covers safe access on small and fishing vessels and places primary responsibility on the person providing the means of access.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: The recommended access hierarchy prioritises a suitable gangway, followed where appropriate by a direct level step, fixed ladder or portable ladder.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: Safe-access arrangements should include secured and maintained gangways, immediately available lifebuoys with suitable lines and control of mooring-line slack at crossing points.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: Mooring and access risk depends on vessel type, equipment design and condition, line material and load, berth, tide, weather, work positioning, communication and crew competence.

rows.source: MCA mooring, anchoring and safe-access controls
rows.verified: MCA mooring evidence is vessel-, equipment-, operation-, berth-, crew- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
